bugClass.title: Startup validation misses database writability
bugClass.cause: Startup validates database file privacy and identity properties but does not verify that the process can write to the initialized database or its journal. The database can therefore open read-only and fail on each runtime write; an HTTP error boundary may swallow or fail to log the write error, returning an opaque 500.
bugClass.criteria: Include a site when startup checks database path ownership, permissions, symlink/link count, or existence but omits a write-capability check for the database and relevant journal; the file can consequently be opened read-only and runtime mutations fail. Also include sites where such runtime storage failures are caught by an HTTP handler and converted to an unlogged or opaque 500, even if the permission check is implemented elsewhere.

candidates.evidence: At resourceDatabase.ts lines 8–18, startup opens the SQLite file and sets WAL mode, then chmods the database file to 0600; the shown code has no write-capability check for the database or journal. However, it does not show an ownership, permission, symlink, link-count, or existence validation that this bug class requires, and the excerpt does not establish that the file can be opened read-only or that runtime writes fail.

Lines 8–20 create/open a SQLite database, chmod the database file to 0600, and initialize schema/WAL settings. The excerpt shows no ownership, symlink, or link-count validation and no write-capability check; it also gives no trigger showing the file can become read-only or runtime writes fail, so the candidate's cause is not established.

Lines 119–137 catch run errors and suppress errors from `recordRunFailure`, but the excerpt does not establish an HTTP handler, SQLite storage failure, or database writability checks; the swallowed error is specifically described as a branch/ref conflict.
Lines 21–22 append a report cleanup log with mode `0o600`, but this excerpt does not establish SQLite usage, startup database checks, or an HTTP error path.
